syllabus_topics: Introduction to algorithm analysis and synthesis
Review of data structures: lists; stacks; queues; priority queues; hash tables; binary search trees; balanced trees
Graph algorithms: elementary algorithms, minimum spanning trees, shortest paths, maximum flows
Introduction to Linear Programming and the Simplex algorithm
Algorithm synthesis techniques: dynamic programming and greedy algorithms
Problem classes P, NP, NP-complete, and NP-hard
assessment_rules: The final grade is calculated as round( 0.5 * p + 0.5 * t ), where p is the practical component and t is the theoretical component. The theoretical component t is the maximum of the normal exam grade (en) or the resit exam grade (er). The practical component p is the average of three mini-project evaluations (p1, p2, p3). Students will be considered not evaluated if they do not submit at least 50% of the assessment components. The normal and resit exams have a minimum passing grade of 6 out of 20. For working students, the final grade is round( max( t, 0.5 * p + 0.5 * t ) ). For the special exam period, the final grade is round( max( ee, 0.5 * p + 0.5 * ee ) ).
bibliography: Thomas H. Cormen, Charles E. Leiserson, Ronald L. Rivest and Clifford Stein, Introduction to Algorithms, Third Edition, ISBN-10: 0-262-53305-7; ISBN-13: 978-0-262-53305-8, September 2009 (main)

degree: Licenciatura em Engenharia Informática e de Computadores - Alameda (LEIC-A)
